method: Handwritten C from retained native instructions; Ghidra target identity/body inspection and original REA export provenance; isolated instruction/C comparison

contract_repairs.native: cdecl force selector, void result; frame gates and elapsed time use DWORD slots
contract_repairs.C: typed direct effect calls with the global 44-byte context; discard the side-effect-only 0x0051e990 call result without a false trap

contract_repairs.native: ECX receiver, five stack arguments, ret 0x14; low byte of randomize argument
contract_repairs.C: explicit RestoreSurfaceContext receiver, signed step/brightness arguments, one randomization byte and preserved adjacent padding

contract_repairs.native: ECX receiver, one buffer selector, ret 4; void result
contract_repairs.C: explicit receiver and selector; complete pixel pointers and RNG/history DWORDs

preserved_behavior: RGB555/RGB565 arithmetic follows original masks and shifts, including red shifted by 11 in both greyscale branches.
Pixels in rows 0..29 and columns outside the chosen signed width limit remain untouched; the unselected buffer remains unchanged.
Both 31-shift feedback registers, derived masks and the 100-slot history preserve exact state and wrap order.
Noise consumes randomness per row, including protected top rows and zero-width rows; optional brightness jitter consumes its own advance.
Effect setup clamps signed step counts to 0..15, writes only the randomization byte, and immediately applies one step.
Frame gates compare full DWORDs; only force == 1 overrides elapsed time, and the 50ms comparison is signed after wrapping addition.
Positive frame counters divisible by 136 trigger nine effect/presentation operations without advancing the frame clock.
City-mode redraw precedes one effect in modes 1, 3, 30, 31, 32 and 73; the native caller consumes no return register from the renderer.
limitations: City renderer 0x0051e990 is a controlled endpoint during comparison; its actual globals, downstream object calls and unresolved contracts still need reconstruction.
COM presentation is simulated. Original frame, timing, presentation and clamp instructions run only in the emulator; no original game process starts.
Pixel buffers in these checks are separate from RNG/context storage, buffer selectors are 0/1, and history indexes start within 0..99.
Other callbacks, exception frames, data code pointers, remaining contracts and the complete C game entry remain unfinished.
Finite offline comparisons do not establish real graphics behavior or a playable independent game.
